app.title: Spatial Action Review — Autonomous EM Oversight
app.summary: A reviewer loads a model's evaluation run: a shipped record set with a model condition, or an uploaded JSON export with an optional zip of image crops. They then set a reliability threshold. The app puts every record into one of four states, depending on whether the model's answer was right and whether the points it predicted cover enough of the labelled objects. A 2×2 ledger counts the four states, and a heatmap shows the failure rate by task and dataset; clicking a cell in either narrows the review queue. The reviewer steps through the queue one record at a time, looking at the image with true and predicted points overlaid beside the question, the answer and the scores. For each record they choose one of four routing decisions and can add a reason. A threshold sweep shows how the counts move as the gate changes, and the decision log can be exported as CSV or JSON.

task.text: Find the model outputs where a correct answer hides an unreliable spatial action, and record a routing decision for each one before the action is used downstream.

data.text: Records from a model evaluation run, one per image region and question. Each has the answer's correctness, the labelled object centroids, the predicted points, recall scores, and an image crop.
data.item: an image crop paired with a question, the model's answer and the points it predicted

stage.text: reviewing a model's outputs after an evaluation run, before its actions are cleared for downstream use

mechanism.text: A threshold slider puts every record into one of four answer-action states. A clickable 2×2 ledger and a task×dataset heatmap both filter the review queue that drives a one-record image audit with point overlays, where the reviewer records a routing decision. Tabs below hold a threshold sweep chart, a table comparing conditions, the decision log with exports, and a side-by-side live re-ask of the open record.

field.text: auditing vision-language model point predictions against labelled objects, as visual analytics for model oversight

workflow.name: triage model outputs one at a time and record a routing decision for each

steps.here: Pick a shipped record set and model condition in the sidebar, or upload an inspector_data.json with an optional zip of crops named <crop_id>.png

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A τ slider sets the object-recall gate. Each record becomes aligned pass, silent failure, action-only pass or blocked, and the ledger shows the count and rate of each

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Clicking a ledger cell picks the state to review (silent failure by default). Clicking a task×dataset heatmap cell narrows the queue to that region, and clicking it again clears it

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: prev/next walk the queue. Each record shows the crop with green crosses on the labelled objects and red rings on the predicted points, a verdict, stray-point flags, and the question, answer and scores

steps.step: decide what happens to each item, with a reason
steps.here: Four buttons record a decision: accept action, escalate for expert review, hold for a stricter gate, or flag for model revision. An optional reason is saved with it, and a counter shows how many records in the queue are signed off
A sweep chart and table show how many actions are cleared, held, or fall in the silent-failure queue as τ moves from 0.05 to 0.95

The review log counts decisions by route, warns when a decision was made under a different τ, and downloads the decisions as CSV or self-describing JSON. The current queue can also be downloaded as CSV

distinctive: Each item has two linked outputs, a text answer and a set of spatial points, and the review targets the case where the answer passes but the points fail
The reliability gate τ is adjustable, and every decision stores the τ it was made under; decisions made under a different τ are flagged as stale rather than re-evaluated
The whole view is encoded in the URL (source, condition, τ, state, cell, open record, theme), so any state can be shared and reopened
The open record can be re-asked live against a served model endpoint, and the new points are shown beside the stored record without changing the audit
Points that land on no labelled object are counted and flagged separately, because the gate measures coverage, not precision
